idea-plugin.name: Fast Compose Preview
idea-plugin.description:
Instant Jetpack Compose previews in Android Studio and IntelliJ IDEA. No compiler, no build, no waiting.

Type in a composable and watch every @Preview update in milliseconds. Your Compose code runs in the Fast Compose runtime, so there is no Gradle build, no Kotlin compiler and no preview process to wait for. It works for Jetpack Compose and Compose Multiplatform.

⚡ Live as you type

  • Previews follow the open Kotlin file and its unsaved text: no save, no build, no manual refresh.
  • Switch files and the preview switches with you; files without a @Preview cost nothing.
  • Previews lay out at a Phone, Foldable, Tablet or Desktop size and scale to fit the panel, so Scaffold screens look as they do on a device. Zoom from the bar below the previews or with Ctrl + mouse wheel.

🖥️ Your layout, your screens

  • A Fast Compose Preview tool window next to Running Devices.
  • Open Preview in Window moves it to its own window, so your code fills one display and your UI the other. The IDE remembers where you put it.

📦 Built for real projects

  • Android and Kotlin Multiplatform: composables, classes and values from other files and modules.
  • expect declarations run their JVM or Android actual.
  • Images and strings from R and Res across modules, with unsaved edits to strings.xml shown right away.
  • Network images with Coil, cached on disk.

🔍 Errors you can act on

  • A logs pane for parse errors, runtime errors and println output; click a line to jump to it, in this file or another.
  • A preview that crashes shows why in the logs, never an empty panel.
  • Report Issue opens a prefilled GitHub issue in one click.

🪶 Light on your IDE

  • Nothing runs while the preview is hidden or minimized.
  • Files and resources are read from the IDE's own file tree, only when a preview needs them.

Good to know

  • Previews run in an interpreter: Compose and Kotlin APIs that Fast Compose doesn't support yet are reported in the logs instead of rendering.
  • Multi-preview annotations (e.g. @PreviewLightDark, your own annotation classes) and @PreviewParameter are not supported yet.
  • Network images are downloaded from the URLs in your code.
